::: {.a11y-lede}
PEN is built for the disability community. Making it work for everyone is part
of the job, not an extra.
:::

## Our goal {.a11y-goal}

<p class="a11y-goal-mark" aria-hidden="true">AA<small>WCAG 2.2</small></p>

<p class="a11y-big">PEN is built to meet WCAG 2.2, Level AA.</p>

WCAG is the main international standard for accessible websites, and AA is the
level most laws and organizations ask for. We treat it as the minimum, and we
test against it.

## What you can expect

<p class="a11y-intro">Four things hold on every page, whichever way you use PEN.</p>

<ul class="a11y-ways">
<li>
<h3>With a keyboard</h3>
<p>Every page works with a keyboard alone. A thick outline always shows where you are.</p>
<p>The keys you need are in the table below.</p>
</li>
<li>
<h3>With a screen reader</h3>
<p>Pages have clear headings and labeled sections, so you can jump to what you need.</p>
<p>Use your screen reader's headings list or landmarks list to move around.</p>
</li>
<li>
<h3>With zoom or large text</h3>
<p>Zoom in up to 400% and every page still works, with no side-to-side scrolling.</p>
<p>Text is large and has strong contrast with its background.</p>
<p>The Display button, bottom left on every page, lets you choose dark or high contrast colors, larger text, an easy-to-read font, and more space between lines.</p>
</li>
<li>
<h3>Progress and motion</h3>
<p>Progress is always written in words, like "Completed". Color is never the only clue.</p>
<p>Very little moves. If your device is set to reduce motion, we follow that. You can also turn motion down yourself in Display.</p>
</li>
</ul>

## Keys you will use

<p class="a11y-intro">You can do everything in PEN without a mouse.</p>

<div class="a11y-keys">
<table>
<caption>What each key does in PEN.</caption>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">To do this</th><th scope="col">Press</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><th scope="row">Move to the next link or button</th><td><kbd>Tab</kbd></td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Move to the previous one</th><td><kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd></td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Follow a link or press a button</th><td><kbd>Enter</kbd></td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Open or close a module summary</th><td><kbd>Space</kbd> or <kbd>Enter</kbd></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

## Videos

<p class="a11y-intro">Every video added to PEN follows three rules.</p>

<ul class="a11y-video">
<li><h3>Captions</h3><p>Checked and corrected by a person, not left to auto-captions.</p></li>
<li><h3>Transcript</h3><p>The full text is on the page, so you do not have to download it.</p></li>
<li><h3>No autoplay</h3><p>Nothing plays until you start it, and the player works with a keyboard.</p></li>
</ul>

## For assistive technology users

<details class="a11y-more">
<summary>Technical details</summary>
<ul>
<li>Each page has one main heading, and headings never skip a level.</li>
<li>The navigation, main content, and footer are marked as landmarks, so a screen reader can move between them in one step.</li>
<li>You mark each unit complete yourself with the <strong>Mark unit complete</strong> button under its video, once you have watched the video or read the transcript, so watching is never required. Focus then moves to the words <strong>Unit complete</strong>, and a polite announcement says so.</li>
<li>When a video ends, the page moves to that button and puts focus on it. Nothing is completed for you.</li>
<li>If you opened the site from a navigator link, a bar under the menu says so in words and shows your code. Its notices are announced, and <strong>Turn off</strong> asks before it acts, with <strong>Keep it on</strong> as the first choice. When a navigator finishes a module, a full-screen check-in opens as a dialog: focus starts on its main button, and Escape or <strong>I'll do it later</strong> closes it. The bar also says in words how many check-ins are done, and each step on the home page progress list is written out ("Units done", "Check in now", "Checked in").</li>
<li>Module summaries are native expandable sections, so they work with the keyboard and with screen readers.</li>
<li>There is no separate "skip to content" link. The menu is short, and the landmarks already let you move past it.</li>
<li>Lines of text are kept short so they are easier to follow.</li>
</ul>
</details>

::: {.a11y-report}
## Report a barrier {#report-a-barrier}

<p class="a11y-big">If something on this site does not work for you, tell us. We treat it as a bug.</p>

<p class="a11y-ask">Tell us which page, what you were using (browser, screen reader, or keyboard only), and what happened.</p>

[Email us about a barrier](mailto:hammel@uic.edu?subject=PEN%20accessibility%20barrier&body=Page%3A%20%0ABrowser%20or%20assistive%20technology%3A%20%0AWhat%20happened%3A%20){.a11y-btn-inverse}
:::
